```plato
    // x = XAmplitude * sin(2*pi*XFrequency*t + Phase),
    // y = YAmplitude * sin(2*pi*YFrequency*t).
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lissajous_curve
    Eval(self: Lissajous2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => (self.XAmplitude * ((self.XFrequency * t).Turns + self.Phase).Sin,
                   self.YAmplitude * (self.YFrequency * t).Turns.Sin);

    // r = ( |cos(m theta / 4) / a|^n2 + |sin(m theta / 4) / b|^n3 )^(-1/n1).
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superformula
    RadiusAt(self: Superformula2D, angle: Angle): Number
        => (((angle * self.Symmetry / 4.0).Cos / self.XRadius).Abs.Pow(self.Exponent2)
            + ((angle * self.Symmetry / 4.0).Sin / self.YRadius).Abs.Pow(self.Exponent3))
           .Pow(-1.0 / self.Exponent1);

    //==
    // # Further classical polar curves

    // r = Scale * (1 + 2 cos(2 theta)).
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommaso_Ceva#The_Cycloid_of_Ceva
    RadiusAt(self: CycloidOfCeva2D, angle: Angle): Number
        => self.Scale * (1.0 + 2.0 * (angle * 2.0).Cos);

    // r = Scale * sec(theta / 3)^3.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tschirnhausen_cubic
    RadiusAt(self: TschirnhausenCubic2D, angle: Angle): Number
        => self.Scale * (angle / 3.0).Sec.Cube;

    // r = sec theta + Scale * cos theta.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conchoid_of_de_Sluze
    RadiusAt(self: ConchoidOfDeSluze2D, angle: Angle): Number
        => angle.Sec + self.Scale * angle.Cos;

    // r = (Scale^n * cos(n theta))^(1/n). Precondition: Exponent is non-zero.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinusoidal_spiral
    RadiusAt(self: SinusoidalSpiral2D, angle: Angle): Number
        => (self.Scale.Pow(self.Exponent) * (angle * self.Exponent).Cos)
           .Pow(1.0 / self.Exponent);

    // r = 2 * Scale / cos(theta / 3).
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trisectrix_of_Maclaurin
    RadiusAt(self: TrisectrixOfMaclaurin2D, angle: Angle): Number
        => 2.0 * self.Scale / (angle / 3.0).Cos;

    // The butterfly curve over its full 12-pi period:
    //   x = sin u * f(u), y = cos u * f(u),
    //   f(u) = exp(cos u) - 2 cos(4u) - sin(u / 12)^5,  u = 6 * pi * t.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Butterfly_curve_(transcendental)
    ButterflyFactor(u: Angle): Number
        => u.Cos.Exp - 2.0 * (u * 4.0).Cos - (u / 12.0).Sin.Pow(5.0);

    // The butterfly point at the canonical parameter t.
    Eval(self: ButterflyCurve2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => (self.Scale * (t * 6.0).Turns.Sin * (t * 6.0).Turns.ButterflyFactor,
                   self.Scale * (t * 6.0).Turns.Cos * (t * 6.0).Turns.ButterflyFactor);

    //==
    // # Evaluating the plane spirals and roulettes
    //
    // Closed-form evaluation of the types declared in `curves-shapes.types.plato`.
    // The spirals are `IPolarCurve2D` implementors that carry an explicit `Angles`
    // sweep, so each supplies a `RadiusAt` plus an `Eval` overriding the generic
    // full-turn mapping of the polar section above; the roulettes are written
    // directly in Cartesian form. The shared `CirclePoint` helper is in the arcs
    // section.
    //
    // TODO(interface-gap): an angular curve interface — a curve whose
    // natural parameter is an `Angle`, with a single bridge
    // `Eval(curve, t: Number) => curve.Eval(t.Turns)`. This is NOT a fold gap and
    // the P2 `Reduce`/`MapRange` primitives do not touch it: the block is purely a
    // missing interface surface. The clean fix is `interface IAngularCurve2D` (with the
    // obligation `Eval(self, theta: Angle): Point2D`) plus one bridge, whose
    // natural home is `curves.concepts.plato` alongside the other curve
    // interfaces — a file owned by the curves package, not editable from this
    // library-body pass. Until that interface lands, the roulettes and figure curves
    // below each spell out the `t.Turns` conversion in their own `Eval`.

    //==
    // # Spirals and transition curves

    // r = StartRadius + GrowthRate * theta, theta in radians.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archimedean_spiral
    RadiusAt(self: ArchimedeanSpiral2D, angle: Angle): Number
        => self.StartRadius + self.GrowthRate * angle.Radians;

    // The point at the swept angle, overriding the generic full-turn mapping.
    Eval(self: ArchimedeanSpiral2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => self.CartesianPositionAt(self.Angles.Lerp(t));

    // r = StartRadius * exp(GrowthRate * theta), theta in radians.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logarithmic_spiral
    RadiusAt(self: LogarithmicSpiral2D, angle: Angle): Number
        => self.StartRadius * (self.GrowthRate * angle.Radians).Exp;

    // The point at the swept angle, overriding the generic full-turn mapping.
    Eval(self: LogarithmicSpiral2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => self.CartesianPositionAt(self.Angles.Lerp(t));

    // r = Scale * sqrt(theta), theta in radians. Precondition: theta >= 0.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermat%27s_spiral
    RadiusAt(self: FermatSpiral2D, angle: Angle): Number
        => self.Scale * angle.Radians.Sqrt;

    // The point at the swept angle, overriding the generic full-turn mapping.
    Eval(self: FermatSpiral2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => self.CartesianPositionAt(self.Angles.Lerp(t));

    // The clothoid is parameterized by signed arc length, so its arc length is
    // just the width of Domain.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_spiral
    ArcLength(self: Clothoid2D): Number
        => self.Domain.Extent.Abs;

    // The canonical [0,1] parameter reached after walking the given distance
    // from the start. Precondition: ArcLength > 0.
    ParameterAtLength(self: Clothoid2D, length: Number): Number
        => length / self.ArcLength;

    // The point reached after walking the given distance along the curve.
    PointAtLength(self: Clothoid2D, length: Number): Point2D
        => self.Eval(self.ParameterAtLength(length));

    // `Eval(Clothoid2D, Number)` is at the foot of the spirals section. It sidesteps both
    // of the blockers the old TODO here recorded: quadrature of the tangent
    // angle replaces the truncated Maclaurin series that degraded over real
    // arc-length spans, and there is no guessed scaling because the type's own
    // doc comment pins the argument — curvature is s / Flatness^2 and the
    // parameter IS signed arc length, so the tangent angle is s^2 / (2
    // Flatness^2) and nothing is left to choose.

    // The involute of a circle: x = R(cos theta + theta sin theta),
    // y = R(sin theta - theta cos theta), theta in radians.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Involute
    Eval(self: CircleInvolute2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => (self.Radius * (self.Angles.Lerp(t).Cos
                                  + self.Angles.Lerp(t).Radians * self.Angles.Lerp(t).Sin),
                   self.Radius * (self.Angles.Lerp(t).Sin
                                  - self.Angles.Lerp(t).Radians * self.Angles.Lerp(t).Cos));

    //==
    // # Roulettes (rolling-circle curves)

    // x = R(theta - sin theta), y = R(1 - cos theta), theta in radians.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cycloid
    Eval(self: Cycloid2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => (self.Radius * (self.Angles.Lerp(t).Radians - self.Angles.Lerp(t).Sin),
                   self.Radius * (1.0 - self.Angles.Lerp(t).Cos));

    // x = (R+r)cos t - r cos((R+r)/r t); y = (R+r)sin t - r sin((R+r)/r t).
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epicycloid
    Eval(self: Epicycloid2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => (t.Turns.CirclePoint(self.FixedRadius + self.RollingRadius)
            - ((self.FixedRadius + self.RollingRadius) / self.RollingRadius * t.Turns)
                  .CirclePoint(self.RollingRadius))
           .ToPoint;
```
